fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description: Detects PowerShell download and execution cradles.
fields.name: PowerShell Download and Execution Cradles
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and ((tgt.process.cmdline contains ".DownloadString(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".DownloadFile(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "Invoke-WebRequest " or tgt.process.cmdline contains "iwr ") and (tgt.process.cmdline contains ";iex $" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "| IEX" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "|IEX " or tgt.process.cmdline contains "I`E`X" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "I`EX" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "IE`X" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "iex " or tgt.process.cmdline contains "IEX (" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "IEX(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains "Invoke-Expression")))
